name: four-ideas
title: Four Ideas, One Release
html:
Four Ideas, One Release

1Sync, Reason, ActOne loop, like a person in a browser. Only Reason costs tokens. Coupled to media types, never to a domain.
2Hypertext-drivenFielding, 2008: if hypertext doesn’t drive it, it isn’t a REST API. Period.
3Controls in the answerThe human Web always kept them there. The machine Web moved them into docs. HEART rejoins them.
4Zero tokensHightower: infer once, then run plain code. The controls in each answer keep “once” true.

Next: one release, walked once with Claude, then replayed with no model.
say: Four ideas, and then we watch them run. One: a generic client runs one loop, read, think, act, and only thinking costs tokens. Two: Fielding says an API that isn't driven by hypertext isn't REST, period. Three: the human Web has always kept the controls in the answer, and the machine Web moved them out into docs; HEART puts them back. Four: Hightower says infer once, then run plain code, and Fielding's controls are what keep once true. Now the release itself.
